head: pr17421-r17
report:
Use absolute imports.

## Pin the cell's URL roots after the request env is applied, not before (P1: wrong-session writes and reads)

**File:** `packages/coding-agent/src/eval/py/runner.py:2700`, used by `prelude.py:41-44` (`_omp_url_roots`).

**Mechanism.** `_handle_request_async` runs `_CURRENT_URL_ROOTS.set(os.environ.get("PI_EVAL_LOCAL_ROOTS"))` at line 2700. The request's own env patch is applied later, by `_apply_request_runtime(req)` at line 2718, which writes `PI_EVAL_LOCAL_ROOTS` from `req["env"]` (the host's `buildManagedKernelEnvPatch`, `executor-base.ts:351/360`). So every cell pins the roots of the *previous* request. `_omp_url_roots()` now prefers the pinned value over the environment, which produces two failures:
- `write("local://…")` lands in the previous session's `local` directory.
- `_artifact_file` sends the previous session's artifact directory as `root` to `__artifacts_ready__`, so `read("artifact://N")` returns the old session's artifact N.

The patch claims "a cell suspended across a session re-adoption still reads the artifacts directory it was started with". The probe shows the opposite: the first cell after a re-adoption is the one that gets the wrong directory. The very first cell in a kernel escapes only because the pinned value is `None` and the code falls back to the environment.

**Trigger.** Drive the real `runner.py` with the real `PYTHON_PRELUDE`. Send two cells whose `env.PI_EVAL_LOCAL_ROOTS` differ (OLD, then NEW), as the host does after a session switch on a reused kernel. Probe: `scratch/roots-write.ts`, run with `bun …/roots-write.ts` from `packages/coding-agent`.

```
{"type": "stdout", "id": "cell-old", "data": "old session cell wrote .../roots-xNFm7T/OLD/local/a.txt\n"}
{"type": "stdout", "id": "cell-new", "data": "new session cell wrote .../roots-xNFm7T/OLD/local/b.txt\n"}
OLD/local: [ "b.txt", "a.txt" ]
NEW/local: []
```

A smaller version prints the pinned value directly. Send `runner.py` two frames with OLD and then NEW roots:
```
cell1 pinned= None env= {"artifact":"/sessions/OLD","local":"/sessions/OLD/local"}
cell2 pinned= {"artifact":"/sessions/OLD","local":"/sessions/OLD/local"} env= {"artifact":"/sessions/NEW","local":"/sessions/NEW/local"}
```

**Fix.** Set `_CURRENT_URL_ROOTS` after `_apply_request_runtime(req)` has run.

## Stop the session-wide Python bridge fallback from running any tool for a dead or foreign run (P1: run scoping lost)

**File:** `packages/coding-agent/src/eval/py/tool-bridge.ts:199`, together with line 292.

**Mechanism.** `registerPyToolBridge` now also writes `sessionRegistrations.set(sessionId, entry)`. The unregister closure never removes that entry; only `shutdownInvalidatedSession` does. The request handler looks up `registrations.get(registrationKey) ?? sessionRegistrations.get(sessionId)` for **every tool name**. The gate at line 195 rejects only an *empty* `run`. A request that carries a **stale** run id, for `bash`, `write`, `agent` or anything else, therefore skips the run check and executes under the newest cell's entry: its `toolSession`, its `signal` and its `emitStatus`. That holds even after every cell has ended.

Before the patch, the fallback was `registrations.get(sessionId)`. Keys there are always `${sessionId}:${runId}`, so that lookup never matched, and a stale run got `No active Python tool bridge session`. The patch's own comment says "Everything else still has to say which cell it is"; a cell that has ended is now accepted for everything.

**When it happens in practice** [INFERENCE from Python semantics, not run end to end]: work a cell leaves running inherits its run id when it was started with `asyncio.create_task(...)` or `asyncio.to_thread(...)`, because both copy the context. A cancelled cell's leftover task would then keep running tools. The tools would get the next cell's abort signal, and their status would be reported against that next cell.

**Trigger.** Probe: `scratch/pybridge-stale-run.test.ts`, run with `bun test …/pybridge-stale-run.test.ts` from `packages/coding-agent`. It registers run-A and unregisters it (the cell ends). It then POSTs `{session, run:"run-A", name:"bash"}`, registers and unregisters run-B, and POSTs again with run-A.

```
after A ended, no cell running: {"ok":true,"value":"bash-done"} [ "bash ran args={\"command\":\"rm -rf x\"} signalAborted=undefined" ]
cell A thread after B ended: {"ok":true,"value":"bash-done"} logB= [ "bash ran args={\"command\":\"echo from-A\"} signalAborted=false" ]
```

The second line shows cell A's call running on cell B's tool session with B's signal.

**Fix.** Consult `sessionRegistrations` only when `name === EVAL_ARTIFACTS_READY_BRIDGE_NAME`.

**Smaller issue (not measured):** a kernel can shut down without passing through `shutdownInvalidatedSession`, for example per-call mode or disposal. Its `sessionRegistrations` entry, and the `ToolSession` it holds, then stays until the process exits.

---

The time budget covered only the eval/artifact-readiness part of the diff. The session-manager, lease and fork-on-resume changes (about 2,500 lines of `session-manager.ts`) were not reviewed.

**Verdict:** not safe to merge. Python cells read and write the previous session's `artifact://` and `local://` directories after a session switch, and the bridge fallback lets a cell that has ended run any tool.
